svg.title: The Lagrange error bound sits above the actual error
svg.desc: On -1.6 to 1.6, a dashed curve x to the fourth over 24, the Lagrange error bound for cos x and its second-degree Taylor polynomial about 0, with the region under it lightly shaded, and a solid curve, the actual error |cos x minus (1 minus x squared over 2)|, which stays below it. At x = 1 the bound is about 0.0417 and the actual error about 0.0403.

text.tspan: For cos x and P₂(x) = 1 − x²/2, the actual error never rises above the bound.
The bound uses the largest size the next derivative can have, so it is safe but larger than the error.
